The decision applies to how the body of water is officially identified by US authorities, but Trump has no power to make Canada adopt the new name. The move follows Trump's earlier decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” for use by the US government.

However, the actual wildlife event showed the goose fighting back successfully. The eagle eventually abandoned its pursuit, and the image backfired diplomatically. This incident highlights the administration's social media efforts often failing.

title: From washing utensils in Kolkata to a career-best 167: Shahbaz's cricket journey
description: Shahbaz Ahmed left civil engineering studies in Haryana to chase cricket dreams in Kolkata, 1,500km from home. Facing financial hardship, he washed dishes and lived in modest club quarters while training. His breakthrough came with Tapan Memorial, followed by Bengal, IPL and India selection. After slipping from contention, Shahbaz returned strongly with 167 runs and 3/20 for East Zone.

title: Vince Young’s rise, NFL fallout, bankruptcy and road to redemption
description: From a turbulent childhood to college football acclaim, Vince Young’s story is a testament to perseverance. While his NFL stint with the Tennessee Titans was full of challenges and financial hardships, Young has reclaimed control of his life. Now, he channels his efforts into being a dedicated father, aiming to cultivate a lasting, positive impact for his three kids.

title: Rs 1.1 lakh cr to Rs 2.1 lakh cr: Why cost of 1st bullet train project has doubled
description: The bullet train project is also becoming a platform for India's own high-speed rail ambitions. BEML and ICF are developing India's first indigenous high-speed trainset, with the first expected to roll out in 2027. The trains are being designed for operating speeds of around 250 kmph, with a design speed of 280 kmph.

title: US Marines unveil new role for infantry in age of drones; how Indian Army is transforming
description: The US Marine Corps is rethinking its infantry strategies to adapt to a future dominated by drone warfare. Meanwhile, India is enhancing its military capabilities by incorporating advanced drones and counter-drone technologies within its ground forces. The Army is creating specialized units and providing training to manage a structured approach to drone operations.

title: Cedric Tillman’s rise brought hope, struggles raised doubts and end stunned fans
description: With the roster deadline looming, the Cleveland Browns have parted ways with wide receiver Cedric Tillman. This decision reflects the team's commitment to younger, more promising talents at the position. Despite Tillman's adequate performance, it wasn't enough to keep him on the roster. The Kansas City Chiefs could see potential in him as a budget-friendly option, leaving Tillman to seek new opportunities elsewhere in the league.

title: Nearly one million Indians stuck in US green card backlog; EB-2 wait could stretch to 179 years
description: In the United States, close to one million Indians are bogged down by long-lasting green card backlogs, representing a staggering seventy-nine percent of applicants in these categories. Some Indian professionals may face wait times soaring to an unbelievable 179 years. This issue arises from annual visa caps and per-country limits, highlighting the urgent need for reforms to alleviate the distressing delays faced by skilled workers.

title: Happy Raksha Bandhan 2026: Images, wishes, messages, quotes, pictures and greeting cards
description: Raksha Bandhan honors the profound bond that exists between siblings, where brothers and sisters exchange heartfelt wishes and messages to celebrate their connection. This festival promotes virtual connections, allowing loved ones to express their affection despite physical distance. The sacred rakhi thread symbolizes an unwavering promise of love and safety, enriching sibling ties through treasured memories and joyful experiences.

The S-400 system demonstrated its long-range strike capability during Operation Sindoor. It successfully intercepted a large Pakistani aircraft over 300 kilometers away. India's air defence network has expanded with additional S-400 system deliveries.

title: A Hawaii retreat, staff revolt, and weak AI: How Meta's 60% layoffs plan came apart
description: Meta explored cutting some teams by up to 60% and handing their work to AI agents under a plan code-named Project OT. Hatched at Mark Zuckerberg's Hawaii retreat, it involved two layoff waves, pods of three replacing traditional teams, and keystroke tracking to train AI models. Staff revolted, internal sentiment fell from 74% to 55%, and Meta's own data showed the AI wasn't delivering promised productivity gains.

title: The big IT shake-up: Hiring in GCCs outpaces traditional tech; who gets the job?
description: Global Capability Centres or GCCs which are essentially specialised offshore units of multinational companies are fast absorbing talent from the traditional IT sector. The trend suggests that India’s GCCs are emerging as an increasingly important engine of technology hiring.

title: Colombo draw tastes like defeat as Sri Lanka dent India's WTC final hopes
description: India let a golden chance slip in Colombo as Sri Lanka's remarkable lower-order resistance forced a draw, hurting the visitors' World Test Championship hopes. Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133 capped a sensational series for him, while India's flat tactics and inability to dismiss the tail after dominating the match leaves India with virtually no margin for error for the remaining WTC calendar.

title: New York ski resort built by Chinese-American veteran joins state park
description: In the 1950s, Chinese American Army veteran Joseph Tso bought a mountain property near Ellenville, New York, and developed a hotel and ski area there. The resort became the country’s only Chinese American-owned and operated ski resort. In 2026, the 440-acre Mt. Cathalia property was acquired for $3.3 million and is planned to become part of Minnewaska State Park Preserve.

Apollo 15 astronauts found 4-billion-year-old 'Genesis Rock' on the Moon
description: Apollo 15 astronauts discovered an unusually bright rock near Spur Crater on the Moon.  This sample, known as the Genesis Rock, is an anorthosite and about four billion years old.  Scientists believe it represents a piece of the Moon's primordial crust.  Its mineral composition offers valuable clues about early lunar geological history.  This ancient sample continues to aid understanding of the Moon's evolution.

title: In 1984, Nasa sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
description: Thousands of honeybees travelled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984.  These bees survived microgravity and adapted to their new environment within days.  The mission aimed to observe bee behavior and compare space-built honeycomb.  The bees successfully built approximately 200 cm of honeycomb during the seven-day mission.  Researchers noted differences in cell diameter and wall thickness compared to Earth-made structures.

title: Anthropic tells employees at its San Francisco office to work from home
description: Anthropic asked its employees to work remotely this week due to a potential security guard walkout.  The security contractor, Allied Universal, had warned the AI company about this possibility.  However, the guards' union stated that no strike authorization vote has occurred.  This action by Anthropic appears to be a precautionary measure against an unconfirmed threat.  The company is preparing for a potential initial public offering soon.
